title: Bring a friend
intro: Trade a Pokémon. Take the other side of the cabinet. Send a message, share a record, watch a team keep the next moment alive. This edition follows the things we did together—and the small machines that made them possible.

/zones/games/.title: The other player changes the game
/zones/games/.intro: Trade through the original Cable Club, learn the arcade’s six-button language, then compare the machines on the couch. The next move belongs to somebody else.

/zones/music/.title: A loop. A sequence. A reason to listen again.
/zones/music/.intro: Try a three-record French-house route, follow a sample to its source and build a timed side. These guides give the next listen a particular job.

/zones/tv-movies/.title: An evening takes some arranging
/zones/tv-movies/.intro: Choose a rental, check the broadcast schedule and find out what a summer release calendar actually promises. A screen is only one part of making an evening happen.

/zones/tech-toys/.title: Make the small machine do the work
/zones/tech-toys/.intro: Budget an MP3 player’s 32 MB, compare two ways to type HELLO and trace a file between computers. Try the limits as well as reading about them.

/zones/culture/.title: Give the familiar picture its full story
/zones/culture/.intro: Follow the team behind the 1999 final, identify an actual 1997 electronic pet and read the authorship behind a garment. The details make the memory more interesting.

/zones/fashion/.title: The garment carries a reference
/zones/fashion/.intro: Trace FUBU’s authorship, the grunge runway and the route through a real mall. Read the garment before treating its logo as the whole story.

/zones/internet-culture/.title: Make a page. Leave a trace.
/zones/internet-culture/.intro: Make a homepage, join the invented webring and leave a local guestbook preview. Then follow the browser, shared desk and connection behind the visit.

/zones/transparent-tech/.title: A new shell, a new routine
/zones/transparent-tech/.intro: Look through a shell, then ask what changed in use. Compare the iMac’s file handoff, a handheld’s power requirements and the objects carried between rooms.
